obraz: Halfway up the hill the legs find a strength the flat road never asked for.
proc: Resistance of the hill brings out a bodily strength that was already there.
Resistance calls out a bodily strength already there.

obraz: After months of practice, you answer in the new language without translating first.
proc: Long earlier practice shows as a result that came at its own pace.
Long earlier work shows as a result at its own time.

obraz: The potato forgotten in the cupboard has put out white shoots.
proc: New fragile life begins unforced; also something completing itself unseen.
Shut away and unwatched, it grew on its own inside.

obraz: The bee leaves the clover carrying its dust to the next flower.
proc: Something of value is carried on and passed to the next, growing by moving.
What is carried on and passed along is what bears fruit.

obraz: You turn down the praise and say whose work it was.
proc: Takes the honest side and knowingly gives up the praise.
Keeping to the truth knowingly costs one's own credit.

obraz: The reply is written in a single breath, and your thumb stops above the send button.
proc: A rushed move is stopped just before it is made.
The rushed move is halted just before it is made.

obraz: The coins dropped in the jar each evening are, one day, the fare.
proc: Small acts done long before show one day as a result.
Small acts done long before ripen into a result.

obraz: The recipe card is in another hand, with one change added in yours.
proc: Something handed down, carried on with one's own change.
Something inherited is carried on with one's own change.

obraz: Halfway through the dishes a song comes on, and you both join in.
proc: Shared joy in the middle of a task, not at its end.
Shared lightness in the middle of a chore.

obraz: The child struggles with the zip, and you wait while they try again.
proc: A small one's attempt is given room rather than forced.
A small beginner is given room rather than forced.

obraz: The cold of the river at your ankles stops you before the current does.
proc: A sharp sensation at the edge stops the step and protects.
A sharp sting at the edge stops the step before harm.

obraz: The umbrella turns inside out in the gust; you push it back and walk on.
proc: It bends under the gust, is restored and goes on unbroken.
An outside gust wrecks the umbrella; it is pushed back and survives.

obraz: The table has moved through three homes and still stands in the kitchen.
proc: A thing carried along from home to home and kept.
A thing carried on from home to home.

obraz: Dinner is burnt, and the table laughs over bread and cheese.
proc: Shared laughter in the middle of things despite the failed plan.
Shared joy in the middle of a failed dinner.

obraz: The seedling droops for a week in its new pot, then puts out one leaf.
proc: Fragile new growth appears after being left time and room.
Fragile life given a new place slowly begins to grow.

obraz: Your foot is already off the kerb when the horn sounds.
proc: A move already begun is stopped at the threshold by a warning.
A sharp stop at the threshold just as the move is made.

obraz: The tall grass lies flat in the wind and is standing again by evening.
proc: Bends flat under strain and stands again, unbroken.
It bends under the force and does not break.

obraz: The stream runs in the bed the old river cut.
proc: The new follows a course inherited from what came before.
The new water follows a course handed down by the old.

obraz: On the first warm day every door on the street stands open.
proc: A shared lightening across the whole street as warmth arrives.
A shared lightening as the whole street opens up.

obraz: The eider plucks her own down to line the nest.
proc: Care that prepares room for new life, at the carer's own cost.
Care prepares room for new fragile life.

obraz: One person says the name no one has said all evening, and the table goes quiet.
proc: A spoken name arrives and changes the whole table.
A spoken name arrives and changes the room.

obraz: The runner slows to a walk on the hill and does not stop.
proc: Endures the strain by yielding pace without breaking off.
Under strain the runner yields but does not break off.

obraz: You read the same message again in the morning, and it says something else.
proc: After night turns to morning the same thing reads differently.
After night turns to morning the same thing reads differently.

obraz: The flight is cancelled at the gate, and the queue turns round as one.
proc: An outside force breaks the plan for everyone at once.
The plan is cancelled from outside at the last moment.

obraz: Two people walk side by side, and neither could say who set the pace.
proc: Two move in a common rhythm and neither sets it.
Two share one rhythm that neither forced.

obraz: Said aloud, the plan sounds different from the one in your head.
proc: Speaking the thing aloud changes what it means.
Speaking the thing aloud changes what it is.

obraz: A parcel sits on the step, taped shut, with no sender's name.
proc: A closed container holds something that is not yet known.
A closed vessel whose contents and origin are not yet known.

obraz: You turn the map on your phone, and the street falls into place.
proc: One turn and the same street suddenly looks different and clear.
One turn and the same street is seen in a new way.

obraz: A power cut ends the video call and takes the unsaved slide with it.
proc: An uninvited outside event breaks things off and takes something with it.
An outside force breaks the work and shows what is lost.

obraz: Two people carry a long mirror through the doorway, one pausing as the other turns.
proc: Two progress only by matching each other's timing.
Two move one load by adjusting to each other.

obraz: The raven calls once from the roof, and everyone at the door looks up.
proc: A single sound arrives and turns everyone's attention.
A single call arrives and everyone responds.

obraz: There is a recording of your own voice, and you cannot recall what it says.
proc: Something exists but its content is not known yet.
The content exists but is not yet known.

obraz: The tide has turned, and the same boats now point the other way.
proc: A turn after which the same things point the opposite way.
A turn after which the same things face the other way.

obraz: One minute of hail, and the washing on the line is on the ground.
proc: A brief outside force knocks down what was set up.
Hail from outside knocks down what was set up.

obraz: Two swans cross the lake, and the gap between them never changes.
proc: Two move together keeping a constant shared rhythm.
Two move together in an unchanging shared rhythm.

obraz: The path across the grass is on no plan; it is where everyone actually walks.
proc: A way made simply by people walking it.
A road made only by people walking it.

obraz: The tide pool at dusk moves once, and whatever moved does not show itself.
proc: Something moves under the surface and is sensed, not seen.
Something is there but does not show itself yet.

obraz: A new document is open, and the cursor blinks on the first line.
proc: An open empty space where nothing is written yet.
An empty page with nothing written yet.

obraz: The phone is at two per cent, and you send the one message that matters.
proc: Scarcity forces the choice of what is truly needed.
Scarcity forces the choice of what is truly needed.

obraz: You hear your own phrase come out of a friend's mouth and learn how it sounds.
proc: One learns about oneself through another person, as a mirror.
One learns about oneself through another's mouth.

obraz: On the long drive you miss your turning because the road was so easy to follow.
proc: The going itself carries one past where one meant to go.
The easy road no longer leads where one meant to go.

obraz: The door opens on its chain, just far enough to see who is knocking.
proc: Guarded openness: open enough to see, not letting everything in.
Open enough to see, guarded enough not to let all in.

obraz: One wall in the new flat is still bare, without a single nail hole.
proc: An unmarked surface with no sign on it yet.
A bare wall with no mark yet.

obraz: One seat is left on the last bus, and two of you are still on the pavement.
proc: There is not enough for both; lack presses on the two.
There is not enough for both, and the lack presses.

obraz: A friend copies the way you tap your foot, and you had never noticed it.
proc: One sees one's own habit through another person's imitation.
One sees oneself through another person.

obraz: After the first hour of walking your feet stop asking how far it is.
proc: A rhythm found only by continuing to move.
The rhythm of the road is found only by walking.

obraz: The phone is silenced for the night, with three numbers allowed to ring through.
proc: A guard that shuts out the world but lets a chosen few through.
A guard that shuts out most and lets a few through.

obraz: Fresh snow lies on the field, and nothing has crossed it yet.
proc: An untouched surface with no mark on it yet.
An unmarked surface where nothing has been written.

obraz: The birch on the lava field grows no taller than the rock that shelters it.
proc: Growth is limited by a constraint; the rock also stands as shelter.
Growth is limited to what the constraint allows.

obraz: In the dark window of the train your own face sits among the other passengers.
proc: One sees one's own face among other people, in a mirror.
One sees oneself among other people as in a mirror.

obraz: The phone light finds the dropped key, and beside it a long-lost earring.
proc: A small light reveals something that had been there all along.
A small light reveals something that was there all along.

obraz: The geese feed with one head always raised.
proc: Constant watchfulness guarding the others.
One always keeps watch while the others feed.

obraz: The candle kept for a special evening has never been lit.
proc: A thing kept unused, its value never put into motion.
A thing saved and never used gives nothing.

obraz: The waterfall has become a wall of ice, its last streams held against the rock.
proc: Moving water has stopped and is held as it is.
Flowing water is stopped and held in place.

obraz: Your foot finds the brake as the car ahead drifts, before you know why.
proc: The body senses and acts before it can be explained.
The body senses the danger before it can be explained.

obraz: The new bulb in the hallway shows a crack that was always in the ceiling.
proc: A light gives shape to something that was always there.
Light reveals what was there all along.

obraz: The cloud lifts, and you see how far up the slope you already are.
proc: In the clear light one sees where one stands.
Light returns and shows where one stands.

obraz: The battery you never use is flat on the day you need it.
proc: What is left standing unused has lost its strength.
What is left unused loses its strength.

obraz: A chain of bubbles rises through the dark water, then stops beneath the clear ice.
proc: Rising movement is stopped and held in view under the ice.
Rising movement is stopped and held in view under ice.

obraz: You turn back at the door, sure something is left behind, before you know what.
proc: Something is sensed before it can be named or explained.
Something is sensed before it can be named.

obraz: One match in the cave shows the wall an arm's length away and no further.
proc: A small flame reveals only what is near.
A small flame reveals only a small circle.

obraz: The curtains open, and the colour you chose by lamplight is another colour.
proc: The turn to daylight makes the same thing look different.
When daylight comes the same thing looks different.

obraz: The pool cut off from the river clouds over while the river runs clear.
proc: What stops moving spoils while what flows stays clear.
What stands still spoils while what moves stays good.

obraz: A drop has frozen at the tip of an icicle, just before it falls.
proc: A movement halted and held just as it is.
A moving drop is stopped and held as it is.

obraz: The swell lifts the boat before any wave can be seen.
proc: A hidden movement of water is felt before it is seen.
A hidden movement under the surface is felt before it is seen.

obraz: You bring a dish to the shared dinner and leave with a plate of someone else's cooking.
proc: Giving and receiving between people without counting.
Something is given and something received between both sides.

obraz: The sun comes round to the window, and every fingerprint on the glass shows.
proc: The sun simply shines and everything on the glass shows.
Sunlight simply shines and shows everything.

obraz: The lid holds, and holds, and gives under your grip.
proc: Resistance gives way to bodily force.
Resistance gives way to bodily force.

obraz: The lift stops between floors, and the building goes on humming around it.
proc: Something that was moving has stopped and is held in place.
A moving thing stops and is held between while all else goes on.

obraz: The dough rests under a tea towel, and by morning it has doubled.
proc: Covered and left alone, it completes itself within.
Under cover it grows by itself until ready.

obraz: The borrowed book comes back with a bar of chocolate on top.
proc: An exchange between two hands with an uncounted extra.
A loan returns with an uncounted gift on top.

obraz: Everyone agreed in the corridor; on the form there is one name, and it is yours.
proc: One alone stands by the word in writing and bears the cost.
One person alone takes the side on record and bears it.

obraz: The salmon climbs the falls one leap at a time.
proc: Raw strength against resistance, though also progress step by step.
The way is made leap after leap.

obraz: The tree planted as a sapling beside the bench now shades the place where you sit.
proc: What was planted long ago has ripened into a result over time.
What was planted long ago now gives its result.

obraz: The broken bone knits under the cast, and nothing can be seen of it.
proc: Something completes itself inside, enclosed and unseen.
Completion happens inside, unseen from outside.

obraz: Someone has remembered how you take your coffee.
proc: A small uncounted attention given from one person to another.
An uncounted attention is given from one person to another.

obraz: You tell the referee the ball was out, and your own team loses the point.
proc: Keeps to the truth and knowingly pays the price.
Honesty is kept and the price is paid knowingly.
